Quantities Declared by the Matrix Parametrization

Source: R/mv_summary.R
mv_param_block.Rd

Returns the block that a parameters7 parametrization declares through param_readable(), widened to the parameter vector of the distribution: the Jacobian columns of the parametrization are placed at the positions of its free values in distrib@params, and every other column is zero. An AR(1) covariance, for instance, declares a scale and a correlation, which a summary reports beside the standard deviations.

Usage

mv_param_block(distrib, theta)

Arguments

distrib

A multivariate_distrib() object.

theta

A named list of parameters, already aligned.

Value

NULL where the parametrization declares nothing, or a named list in the shape of the return value of mv_derived(): value, jacobian, transform and block, with the Jacobian as wide as distrib@params, and a logical attribute precision, TRUE when the quantities describe a precision.

Details

A parametrization that declares nothing gives NULL, and the summary is then the result of mv_derived() without it. The label ends in (precision) when the declared quantities describe a precision, because the parametrization itself does not record whether its matrix is a covariance or a precision. They describe a precision when the distribution is inverted and the parametrization is not an inverse one, or the other way round: an inverse parametrization such as parameters7::ar1_inv() declares, with inverse = TRUE, the quantities of the matrix that it inverts, so under an inverted distribution they describe the covariance.

The positions of the free values are found by name: the family names each free value with a prefix followed by the free name, after the location for the gaussian and the Student t and first for the Dirichlet and the multinomial. Where a name does not identify exactly one parameter, the positions after the location are used. A multivariate family written outside this package may have no param property, so the function tests for it with S7::prop_names() and returns NULL when it is absent.

See also

parameters7::param_readable() for what a parametrization declares, mv_append_block() for how the result is joined on, and mv_derived.multivariate_distrib() and mv_own_block() for the consumers.

Examples

# A log-Cholesky covariance declares no block.
d <- mvgaussian1_distrib(2)
theta <- list(mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, sigma_log_L1 = 0, sigma_log_L2 = 0,
              sigma_L2.1 = 0.5)
th <- distributions7:::align_theta(d, theta)
is.null(distributions7:::mv_param_block(d, th))
#> [1] TRUE

# An AR(1) covariance declares a scale and a correlation.
a <- mvgaussian1_distrib(3, parameters7::ar1(3))
th <- as.list(stats::setNames(c(0, 0, 0, 0.1, 0.3), a@params))
pb <- distributions7:::mv_param_block(a, distributions7:::align_theta(a, th))
pb$value
#>     scale       rho 
#> 1.1051709 0.2913126 
pb$transform
#>   scale     rho 
#>   "log" "atanh" 
pb$block
#>                      scale                        rho 
#> "Autoregressive structure" "Autoregressive structure" 

# The Jacobian is as wide as the parameter vector of the distribution, with
# the mean columns zero.
dim(pb$jacobian)
#> [1] 2 5
pb$jacobian[, 1:3]
#>       mu1 mu2 mu3
#> scale   0   0   0
#> rho     0   0   0

# The simplex of a Dirichlet declares its probabilities, whose free values
# come first among the parameters.
dd <- dirichlet_distrib(3)
thd <- list(mean_alr1 = 0.3, mean_alr2 = -0.2, phi = 8)
pbd <- distributions7:::mv_param_block(dd, distributions7:::align_theta(dd, thd))
pbd$value
#>        p1        p2        p3 
#> 0.4260125 0.2583897 0.3155978
